newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.
newsitem.headline: Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.

text.p: FISCHER DENIES DEALS ON MEDIA OWNERSHIP
Deputy Prime Minister, Tim Fischer, denies allegations that the government has done deals with media barons on what they'll be allowed under media ownership reforms.
The Prime Minister has been accused of making special arrangements with Kerry Packer and Rupert Murdoch, particularly in regard to the Fairfax newspaper group.
But Mr Fischer says there has been no deal.
The Democrats want a Senate Inquiry into the allegations, with Leader Cheryl Kernot saying any changes to media ownership must be fully transparent.
Labor Leader Kim Beazley says the Opposition is also concerned and some form of inquiry would be very useful.
SENIOR JUDGE ATTACKS HANSON
Australians are being warned to beware of demagogues, motivated by racial intolerance.
Chief Justice of the Family Court, Alistair Nicholson, says Independent MP, Pauline Hanson's One Nation Party is playing on the fears of disgruntled and disfunctional sections of society.
He says the high media profile of her views are providing an opportunity for bigots to belittle communities they know nothing about.
Speaking at a Melbourne forum on Asian Family Values, the senior judge says Ms Hanson has wrapped herself in the Australian flag in an attempt to appeal to the worst aspects of nationalism.
DISSATISFACTION WITH HOWARD AMONG BACKBENCHERS
A Federal Liberal backbencher says signs of a lack of backbone in the Howard government are contributing to support for Pauline Hanson's One Nation Party.
The Member for the Toowoomba-based seat of Groom, Bill Taylor, says a number of his backbench colleagues are dissatisfied with the Howard government's response to a number of key issues.
Mr Taylor says they're concerned the government is not moving fast enough on these issues.
HEALTH MINISTER ADMITS HE'S IGNORED DEATHS STUDY
Claims the Federal Health Minister is ignoring an Australian study into hospital deaths have been confirmed by the Health Minister himself, who says the study's findings are wrong.
The study, by Dr Ross Wilson, claims eighteen thousnd people die in Australian hospitals each year, four-times the level in the United States.
Dr Wooldridge says he made his decision about the study after talking to the world expert on the issue who's research was followed by Doctor Wilson.
He says the Harvard University expert told him he didn't believe the results of the Australian study.
Dr Wooldridge says he's not going to change health care in Australia because of one study which has been ignored by most of the medical profession.
FIRE ALARMS SHOULD BE IN BEDROOMS
The New South Wales Fire brigade has issued a warning to parents to move smoke alarms out of hallways and into children's bedrooms.
A study by the Victorian University of Technology found that a fire alarm at 85 decibels was not loud enough to wake a sleeping child unless it was actually inside the child's room.
Fire brigade officer, John O'Day says the finding has prompted the New South Wales Fire brigade to alter its usual recommendation that alarms be placed in hallways.
However, Mr O'Day says recent figures on fire related deaths indicate that alarms are having an affect.
TEASING RAIN FOR VIC & NSW FARMERS
Weekend rain in North West Victoria and South West New South Wales has been little more than a teaser for farmers waiting for their autumn break.
Official figures show less than a millimetre fell in Mildura, although Kiamal unofficially recorded 20 millimetres and about 10 millimetres was recorded in some areas around Swan hill.
The weather bureau says anaylsis of the latest climate indicators reveals signs of a developing El Nino event.

The National Climate Centre says important indicators are rapid falls in the Southern Oscillation Index, warming in the Pacific, weakening pacific trade winds, an early finish to the monsoon in Northern Australia and development of dry areas in Southern Australia.
INDUSTRIAL PEACE IN WA BROKEN AGAIN
A second union has broken industrial peace in Western Australia by announcing a 24 hour strike at the Muja power station near Collie.
The news came just hours after 68 workers from the Construction Forestry Mining and Energy union announced an end to a seven day strike at Muja and Kwinana.
Australian Services Union turbine operators met last night and decided to strike until seven o'clock tonight, leaving only one unit running at the station.
Assistant Branch Secretary of the Australian Services Union, Paul Berlinson, says the action shouldn't inconvenience the public.
